transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

After that scare on the highway a few weeks ago, it’s like a switch flipped—I’m going through my life and work, but I can’t feel any real joy or satisfaction in anything right now. I thought I was having a fatal heart attack, and since then, everything just feels completely flat and distant.
Since that incident on the highway, do you find yourself having intrusive, unwanted memories or vivid flashbacks of the event that make you feel as though it is happening all over again?

Yes, it happens constantly and out of nowhere—even during board meetings or while brushing my teeth, I'll suddenly feel like I'm back on that dark road clutching the steering wheel, convinced I'm dying. My chest tightens, my palms sweat, and I have to fight a massive urge to just bolt from the room or call 911.
Since that incident on the highway, has this been going on for more than one month?
No, it hasn't been a full month yet. It has been about three weeks since that scare on the highway, but these feelings have been completely continuous and haven't let up since that day.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were F43.10 and F43.11 (Post-traumatic stress disorder). However, the patient reports that the symptoms have persisted for only three weeks. According to ICD-10 criteria, PTSD requires symptoms to persist for more than one month. Given the acute onset following a traumatic event and the duration of less than one month, the diagnosis of Acute Stress Reaction (F43.0) is now the most appropriate candidate.
